findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts — Same array-based destinationCalendar handling was ported into larkcalendar and office365calendar CalendarService implementations with no tests for single-item, multi-item, or empty-array behavior differences across the three providers

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — Calendar.createEvent` interface now requires `credentialId: number` as a second parameter, but only GoogleCalendarService implements it — LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and the shared base packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (covering iCal/CalDav-style calendars) still declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with no second parameter, silently ignoring the new required interface param (TS structural typing allows this since extra args are simply dropped by callers), so the credentialId-based calendar disambiguation added for Google is absent from all other calendar integrations.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:152 — Same self-referential `find` bug in `deleteEvent` causes `calendarId` to resolve to `undefined` -> falls back to `"primary"`; if the event isn't on the primary calendar, Google returns 404 which the handler treats as `resolve()` (silent success), so a legacy multi-host booking's calendar event is never actually deleted while the app reports the cancellation as successful

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts — Same array-based destinationCalendar handling was ported into larkcalendar and office365calendar CalendarService implementations with no tests for single-item, multi-item, or empty-array behavior differences across the three providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Lark and Office365 calendar providers to treat `destinationCalendar` as an array and to use only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` in `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`). This is nontrivial behavior (empty array => undefined, multi-item => ignores all but first) and it diverges from the new multi-destination logic added elsewhere (e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops destinations). The diff does not add or update any provider-specific tests for these cases; the only visible test change is an e2e fixture update (`apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` sets `destinationCalendar: []`).
